metadata.title: Regularity theorems for Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system
metadata.abstract: We prove several regularity theorems concerning Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system. The main lemma (i.e. ``Decoupling Lemma") says that the component functions of such solutions satisfy the homogeneous Pucci inequalities. This allows us to apply the regularity theory for scalar viscosity solutions for elliptic PDE component-wise to a viscosity solution for the system. As a result of the Decoupling Lemma, we deduce that 2D Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the system are analytic in the interior, and obtain a quantitative partial regularity theorem. We also prove a geometric Harnack inequality for Lipschitz solutions. The Harnack inequality yields a strong maximum principle and half-space Liouville theorem. Another significant consequence of the lemma is a boundary regularity theorem for Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Notably, our theorem does not require any density assumption at the graph boundary, and we do not assume stationarity. This is used to prove a classification theorem for the singular set of a 4D stationary solution on a bounded domain. We also prove an $\varepsilon$-regularity theorem extending a result of the author. To conclude, we survey open problems. As an example, we have included a Bernstein-type theorem for 3D homogeneous entire Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Taken together, our results suggest that viscosity methods are a useful tool for studying the regularity of minimal graphs.
